principles: Treat this artifact as an execution plan, not proof of implemented runtime behavior.
Make milestone boundaries auditable enough that each future milestone can become its own Lattice story.
Expose source/context mapping in the document so research work becomes visible product value.
Preserve existing Lattice conventions for scope, evidence, review, baseline, and ownership semantics.
drivers: The user needs a detailed plan for making Lattice stronger across three interdependent tracks.
Core workflow changes need careful sequencing and future 3-round 2-host validation.
The document should prevent overclaiming while still being executable.

options.name: A: Single roadmap decision document plus NAV registration
pros: Keeps the three strengthening tracks connected through one milestone map.
Makes dependencies, gates, and rollout order easy to audit.
cons: The document will be longer and must be carefully structured to stay readable.
Future implementation stories still need to split work again before coding.

options.name: B: Three separate decision documents, one per strengthening track
pros: Each track would be smaller and locally focused.
Different agents could later own separate tracks with less document-level conflict.
cons: Cross-track dependencies would become easier to miss.
The user asked for one executable scheme with milestones, not three disconnected plans.

options.name: C: Skip the plan and implement the first milestone immediately
pros: Produces runtime behavior sooner for one slice.
Could validate one design assumption quickly.
cons: Violates the current story scope because this story is documentation-only.
Risks implementing local fixes before agreeing on full sequencing and review gates.

chosen: A: Single roadmap decision document plus NAV registration
rationale: Choose one roadmap decision document because the three tracks share scope, evidence, review, baseline, and preflight dependencies. A single source gives future implementation stories a stable milestone map while keeping this story safely documentation-only.

preMortem.scenario: The document reads like aspiration instead of an executable plan.
preMortem.trigger: Milestones lack deliverables, gates, tests, or DONE criteria.
preMortem.consequence: Future developers cannot turn the plan into bounded Lattice stories.
preMortem.mitigation: For every milestone include goal, deliverables, gates, tests, evidence, blockers, and DONE criteria.

preMortem.scenario: The plan accidentally overclaims runtime behavior.
preMortem.trigger: Text says Lattice now blocks or enforces a rule that is only proposed.
preMortem.consequence: Readers may trust non-existent gates and skip necessary implementation work.
preMortem.mitigation: Add explicit status and non-goals sections stating the document is a roadmap only.

preMortem.scenario: The inventory research remains invisible despite the reviewer advisory.
preMortem.trigger: The document cites prior work vaguely without mapping source documents to decisions.
preMortem.consequence: CHK-001 appears complete internally but not from the user-facing artifact.
preMortem.mitigation: Include a Source And Context Mapping table linking related docs to plan sections and decisions.

preMortem.scenario: The plan expands into Layer4 or Authority implementation details prematurely.
preMortem.trigger: Milestones include customerKeyRef, Authority Server, or production-safety work as current scope.
preMortem.consequence: The story violates its scope boundary and mixes future capability into this documentation task.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep Layer4/Authority items as explicit future dependencies or non-goals unless required for a milestone gate definition.
